title: Gold Edges Lower as Traders Assess Prospects for Fed Rate Hike
summary: Gold edged lower ahead of a finely balanced interest-rate decision by the Federal Reserve due later Wednesday.

title: A Slew of Earnings | Closing Bell
summary: Comprehensive cross-platform coverage of the U.S. market close on Bloomberg Television, Bloomberg Radio, and YouTube with Romaine Bostick, Emily Graffeo, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Oil Jumps After Iran Attack, US Stock Futures Dip: Markets Wrap
summary: Crude oil jumped and US equity-index futures fell after fighting erupted in the Middle East, reigniting tensions after several days of calm and reviving concerns over energy supplies.

title: TCBY Executive Director on Resurgence of Frozen Yogurt
summary: TCBY Executive Director Richard Screnci believes there is a place for consumers to watch their health and enjoy eating sweet treats at the same time, as the company looks for more growth opportunities both domestically and abroad. He speaks to Romaine Bostick and Emily Graffeo on Bloomberg's 'The Close.' (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Databricks Co-Founder: IPO a Matter of "When" Not "If"
summary: Databricks Co-Founder and Senior VP of Field Engineering Arsalan Tavakoli sees an endless amount of possibilities in the AI space, but also the need for governance at all levels of the industry as the company waits for the right time to go public. He speaks to Romaine Bostick and Emily Graffeo on Bloomberg's 'The Close.' (Source: Bloomberg)

title: UPS CEO on Return to Growth, Global Economic Outlook
summary: UPS CEO Carol Tomé sees a positive future for the company ahead in large part to the restructuring of priorities away from Amazon delivery, and upgrades to their digital platforms and infrastructure. She speaks to Romaine Bostick on Bloomberg's 'The Close.' (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Barnes and Noble CEO: 'The Odyssey' is Our Best-Selling Book
summary: Barnes and Noble CEO James Daunt is seeing a tremendous resurgence in the business as consumers return to a love of physical book stores, with more to offer like vinyl records and in-store cafes. He also attributes blockbuster Hollywood successes such as 'The Odyssey' being a driving force for Gen Z and older to read more. He speaks with Romaine Bostick and Emily Graffeo on Bloomberg's 'The Close.' (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Rithm Captial CEO on Real Estate Outlook
summary: Rithm Capital Chairman and CEO Michael Nierenberg speaks with Romaine Bostick and Emily Graffeo on Bloomberg's 'The Close' on the company's most recent earnings, as well as looking to the future both in the real estate outlook and overall growth for the company. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for July 29
summary: Oil rebounded after a three-day decline as fresh fighting erupted in the Middle East, with continued threats to energy flows.

title: Bloom Surges on Higher Guidance as Earnings Double Estimates
summary: Bloom Energy Corp. jumped after the fuel-cell maker posted earnings that were more than double expectations and raised full-year guidance for the second consecutive quarter, a sign of rampant demand from data centers.

title: S&P Global’s Shares Drop as Company Misses Profit Estimates
summary: S&P Global Inc. posted quarterly results that fell short of analysts’ average estimate, hurt by factors including the US-Iran War making it harder to boost pricing on contracts for its energy data, news and analysis unit.

title: First Brands Bankruptcy: Lawsuits Around Alleged Fraud Seek to Recoup Billions
summary: The pitch to creditors of bankrupt First Brands goes like this: Stick with us just a while longer, and you’ll get a full recovery as we claw back $2 billion from suing a long list of insiders and business partners who allegedly perpetrated a widespread fraud.

title: NYC Office Project Near Grand Central Lands $1.2 Billion Loan
summary: BXP Inc. has secured a $1.2 billion loan to build a 46-story office tower connected to New York City’s Grand Central Terminal.

title: BlackRock Private Credit Plans Ramp Up in Challenge to Blackstone, Apollo
summary: With direct lending powerhouse HPS in the fold, the world’s largest asset manager is pushing past its own challenges to angle for a large slice of the industry’s future.

title: Ford Cashes In on Sales of High-Margin SUVs
summary: Ford Motor Co. posted earnings ahead of Wall Street estimates and raised its outlook for the second time this year on higher prices and strong sales of high-margin sport-utility vehicles. Erin Keating, Cox automotive executive analyst, says some brands are continuing to cater to customers that want mid-size SUVs, but in the US, there are plenty of buyers for more expensive full-size pickups and SUVs. She speaks on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Emerging Currencies Traded Mixed Amid Oil Plunge, Fed Bets
summary: Emerging-market currencies traded mixed on Tuesday as oil plunged on optimism over US-Iran talks and traders adjusted positions ahead of the Federal Reserve rate decision.

title: Insurers Rally as Stocks Shift from AI Loser to Safe Haven
summary: US insurance-related stocks rallied Tuesday, pushing an industry gauge to close at a record, as artificial intelligence concerns drove traders toward defensive parts of the market.

title: S&P 500 Rises as Oil Drop Outweighs Chip Selloff: Markets Wrap
summary: A rotation that has seen investors bail from high-profile chipmakers in favor of more economically sensitive industries picked up speed, with stocks rising on strong earnings and a drop in oil prices.

title: UPS CEO Says the Amazon Glide Down Is 'Behind Us'
summary: United Parcel Service CEO Carol Tomé says the Amazon glide down "is behind us." The shipping company has been delivering fewer low-margin packages for Amazon. UPS shares fell after its outlook for volume and profit margins underwhelmed investors. Tomé speaks on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Equal-Weight S&P 500 Hits Record; Broad Gains Outweigh Chip Rout
summary: The S&P 500 Index climbed on Tuesday as oil prices continued to slide. Broad gains pushed an equal-weight version of the index to an all-time high even as chipmakers sold off.
